big_idea: We can model ANY real-life situation. Pick a topic from your life, ask a question, build a model.
learning_intention: We are learning to model a real-life situation from our own life.
student_learning_goal: I can model a real-life situation from my own life.
success_criteria: I can pick a real-life situation that interests me.
I can walk through the modelling cycle: situation → question → data → predict → reflect.
I can share my model with the class.
lesson_specific_materials: Syrup jar template for the certificate ceremony
Lesson 5 capstone tracker — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.hook: Now you model YOUR life. Pick a situation. Walk through all 5 steps.
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Maple + Sap Sam. 'Friends — today you become MATHEMATICAL MODELLERS. Pick a real-life situation from your own life. Walk through the cycle: SITUATION, QUESTION, DATA, PREDICT, REFLECT.'

Show the modelling cycle chart. 'You've practiced each step. Today you do them ALL together.'

Show examples:
- 'My class snack box: how many crackers per kid? If 24 kids share 60 crackers, predict each gets 2-3.'
- 'Recess weather: how many sunny days this week? Data → predict.'
- 'Library books I read: 1 book per night × 7 nights = 7 books per week.'

'Pick something from YOUR life. Walk through the 5 steps. We share at the end.'
student_actions: Look at the modelling cycle chart.

steps.instruction: Hand out capstone templates. Children pick a topic and walk through the modelling cycle: write the situation, the question, collect/imagine data, make a prediction, reflect.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say to students: 'Use the template. Walk through ALL 5 steps.'

steps.instruction: Children work for 12-15 minutes individually. Teacher circulates and prompts.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each child. Check completeness — situation, question, data, predict, reflect.

steps.instruction: Stretch challenge: include a refinement based on imagined or real data.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say to extending children: 'Add a refinement step.'

steps.instruction: Gallery walk: children swap templates and read each other's models.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say to students: 'Swap with a partner. Read their model. Tell them ONE thing you liked.'

steps.instruction: Whole-class share: 5-6 children share their model aloud.
steps.teacher_prompt: Pick variety: snacks, sports, friends, daily routines.

differentiation.for_extending: Stretch: invent a model with two refinements.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide picture-supported templates with sentence frames.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Allow them to act out their model with classmates.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: picks a coherent topic; walks through all 5 steps; shares with the class.
formative_check.how_to_record: Tick the capstone tracker per child.

discussion_prompts: What's the most surprising model you saw today?
Why do we use the modelling CYCLE (with arrows back)?
What's something in your life you'll model after this unit?
What's the difference between data and prediction?
consolidation.exit_routine: Each child receives a Junior Mathematical Modeller certificate. Quick whisper: 'My model was about ___'. Maple and Sap Sam say goodbye with a final modelling demo using the class's collective stories.

assessment_in_this_lesson.evidence_collected: Full modelling cycle from a child-chosen topic.
assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 5 captures the C4 summative integration. Children at L4 walk through all 5 steps with a coherent real-life topic.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child can't pick a topic and freezes — repairing the choice paralysis on capstone day
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
The most common Grade-1 trap on the capstone is choice paralysis: the child wants the perfect topic and freezes when given full freedom. They've practiced each step but the open invention paralyses them.

The walkthrough covers the precise moment when a child stares at a blank template.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Child has the capstone template open. Empty. They look stuck.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch beside the child. 'Hard to pick a topic? That's normal. Let's narrow.' Ask: 'What did you do this morning?' 'Brushed teeth, ate breakfast.' 'Pick one. Brushed teeth. Now — math question?' 'How many seconds to brush?' 'YES. Data — actually time it. Predict — 60 seconds. Reflect — was it close?'

Any topic works. The child just needs ONE prompt.

Long-term recovery: provide situation cards as starters.
expected_student_responses: (Confused) Stares at blank template; can't pick.
(Strong) Picks topic and walks through cycle.
(Stretched) Includes a refinement and projects future improvement.
common_misconceptions: I need a perfect topic. (Repair: any topic works.)
Modelling is hard. (Repair: every step we've practised.)
Other people will judge my topic. (Repair: showcase celebrates variety.)
recovery_moves: Use situation cards. Pre-built topics ease choice paralysis.
Ask 'what did you do today?' Anything is a model topic.
Praise the topic regardless of how 'big' it seems.

parts_outline.task: Reflection — would my model need refining?
